claims.text: Catalytic selectivity in transition-metal catalysts is governed by the position of the d-band center relative to the Fermi level.
Alloying a transition metal with a second metal can shift its d-band center.
Shifting the d-band center modulates the adsorption energies of key reaction intermediates.
Changes in intermediate adsorption energies preferentially stabilize one reaction pathway over another.
Alloying alters the catalyst's electronic structure.
The alloy-induced electronic-structure change modifies the adsorption free energies of critical reaction intermediates.
Modified adsorption free energies influence product selectivity by favoring one reaction pathway.
Relative to the pure-metal baseline, the alloyed catalyst will show increased selectivity for the desired product pathway.
The change in product selectivity will correlate with the magnitude of the d-band-center shift.
The proposed d-band-center relationship should hold for catalysts with well-defined surface structures under moderate reaction conditions.
Extreme temperatures or high pressures may invalidate the proposed relationship.
Surface disorder or contamination may invalidate the proposed relationship.
The quantitative relationship between d-band-center shift and selectivity depends on the reaction system, alloy composition, and degree of electronic perturbation.
